project: tbetcegmszzotrwdtqhi (Ops, production), READ ONLY: every request was begin ... rollback, no DDL, no writes
half: 2 of 2: odd indexes of predicate_pairs.json pairs (52 of 104 policies, 47 tables)
method: TEXT: for all 52 policies, oldUsing/oldCheck equal live pg_policies qual/with_check and the md5 signature (52/52); the migration file USING/WITH CHECK, cmd, roles and permissive equal newUsing/newCheck (52/52); newUsingInline/newCheckInline equal newUsing/newCheck with each helper call replaced by its inline body (52/52).

REAL ROWS: per identity, one statement as the default role (postgres, RLS bypassed) inside begin/rollback with request.jwt.claims set: for every policy, count(*) filter (where old), filter (where newInline), and filter (where coalesce(old,false) is distinct from coalesce(newInline,false)), for USING and WITH CHECK. old and new are computed in the same row of the same statement (subquery with offset 0), so both see the same snapshot. Match = equal counts AND 0 rows that differ.

VIRTUAL ROWS (covers empty tables and venues with no rows): every policy evaluated on in memory rows of its own table type built with jsonb_populate_record, one per venue (13), null and a random uuid; text columns also get uppercase, braced, no hyphen, leading space, empty and non uuid spellings; menu_board_screens also varies device_uid over null, a random uuid, every screen uid and the caller. Nothing is written.

HELPER SETS: per identity, for every venue id plus every location id in devices, ops_devices, waitlist_devices, user_locations, menu_board_screens, null, a random uuid and 6 odd text spellings: pos_can_access(text) vs membership in (user_accessible_locations() UNION device parts) and in the inline ids set and in the migration body; pos_can_access(uuid) and pos_can_access(uuid::text) vs the uuids set (inline and migration body); ops_can_write vs ops_writable set; waitlist_can_write vs waitlist_writable set; is_super_admin() vs (select is_super_admin()). The migration helper bodies were read from the migration file itself, so the check covers the SQL that will be created, not only the inline copy.
Devices sign in anonymously (auth.users.is_anonymous true), so each device was run twice: with is_anonymous true (real) and with the task claims template (no flag).
